deities: Lord Sri Balaji Venkateswara (swayambhu - self-manifested idol, presiding)

history.period: 14th century per one source / 500+ years per others (origins not firmly documented - verify)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is NOT in Hyderabad city - it stands at Chilkur village, Moinabad Mandal, Ranga Reddy district, about 25-30 km from central Hyderabad, on the banks of Osman Sagar lake. Documented with the corrected location. The 'Visa Balaji' is one of India's most famous modern pilgrimage stories: devotees, especially students and IT professionals seeking US visas, first walk 11 pradakshinas (circumambulations) around the sanctum to make a wish and return to do 108 if it is fulfilled - the temple reports 75,000 to 1 lakh devotees a week. By local legend the shrine arose when a devotee who could no longer travel to Tirupati prayed here and Balaji appeared to him in a dream. The temple is run by the Chilkur Balaji Temple Trust and is famous for its egalitarian code: NO hundi (donation box), no VIP darshan, no paid sevas - a minister and a labourer stand in the same queue. Entry is free. One source says the deity is 14th century; others say 500+ years - origins not firmly documented, flagged as (verify). Nearest landmarks: Osman Sagar (Gandipet) lake; TSRTC Bus 288D runs from Mehdipatnam.

name: Chilkur Balaji Temple
town: Chilkur (CSV town 'Hyderabad' is WRONG - the temple is at Chilkur village, ~25-30 km from Hyderabad)
town_description: Chilkur is a village in Moinabad Mandal of Ranga Reddy district, Telangana (501504), on the banks of the Osman Sagar (Gandipet) lake, about 25-30 km from central Hyderabad via the Outer Ring Road. An 11th-century inscription records it as an established settlement, but that inscription is not of the present Balaji shrine (per telangana360).

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad - about 35 km (verify).
travel.railway: Hyderabad Deccan (Nampally) railway station - about 30 km (verify).
travel.road: Chilkur Village, Moinabad Mandal; TSRTC Bus No. 288D from Mehdipatnam; drive via Outer Ring Road (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; weekdays mornings are calmest - Fridays and Sundays draw heavy crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Temple open 5:00 AM - 8:00 PM daily; darshan generally 6:00 AM - 1:00 PM and 4:00 PM - 8:00 PM (some sources give 4:00 AM opening and 9:00 PM Sunday closing - verify). No entry fee; no bookings needed; traditional Indian dress recommended.
